newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares slip at noon in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares slip at noon in thin trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share index moved lower in thin trading during the Wednesday morning session, with analysts saying that while the market is approaching its bottom, it lacks strong upward momentum.
The B share index lost 1.54 points or 1.03 percent to 148.16 on flimsy turnover of HK$20 million.
The domestic currency A share index dropped 0.14 points or 0.03 percent to 434.26, with giant newcomer First Automobile Works Car Co Ltd sponging large amounts of funds from the market, brokers said.

"The B share index fell in the morning with dwindling liquidity on the market capping buying interest, but it seems it found some support around the 147-point level where the five-day average passes," a broker at China Guotai Securities said.
"Many B shares look rather cheap at their current levels, which is likely to prevent further falls," the broker said.
But trading would remain stagnant over the short term, barring major market-moving incentives, brokers said.
On the B share market, the worst performer was appliance maker Tsann Kuen, which sank HK$0.17 or 5.28 percent to HK$3.05 on thin volume of 40,550 shares.
Chongqing Huaya Paper was the sharpest loser in the A share market, declining 0.35 yuan or 4.87 percent to 6.84 yuan.
First Auto, which debuted on the Shenzhen exchange with a flotation of 270 million A shares, ended the session at 16.10 yuan against an issue price of 6.80 yuan per share.
The car maker's volume was heaviest at 142 million shares worth 2.1 billion yuan.
Shares are not included in the index calculations on their first day of listing.
